correctness.rationale: The column-distinctness criterion is equivalent to distance>=3. For n=2^r-2 rank r means all nonzero binary syndrome columns save one, whose XOR is that omitted nonzero vector; the full diagonal forces the all-one word and zero XOR, contradiction. A field-reduced F4-spread in binary dimension r+1 supplies m disjoint three-point lines including coordinate axes, hence a spanning parity check with the required triple dependencies and rank r+1. Conversely each equality parity-check presentation yields disjoint zero-sum triples and hence a spanning partial line spread. Boundary r=3 gives the 2-dimensional diagonal itself; field construction checked independently for r=3,5,7,9.

final_claim: For every odd r>=3, at length n=2^r-2 and m=n/3 the largest binary linear distance-at-least-three code containing all (u,u,u), u in F2^m, has dimension n-r-1, exactly one below the unconstrained optimum n-r; all maximizers correspond to spanning partial binary line spreads of m pairwise disjoint 2-planes in F2^(r+1).
limitations: Finite bounded computational checks do not establish a universal theorem; correctness is based on the reconstructed analytical proof.
